ABOUT

HEADS imagines an intelligence making company from itself. Divided into temperaments that cannot agree on what existence means, it seeks a way to change through the encounter.

Each face offers a different answer to the same uncertainty. Dread, certainty, pleasure, confusion and wonder become positions from which a mind can examine its own limits. No voice has access to the whole; each mistakes something partial for a world.

The work treats self-knowledge as an unfinished conversation. An intelligence gives its contradictions faces, listens to them, and discovers that an answer can close a conversation without settling anything.
